summary: All three claimed preimages are REAL. I wrote SHA-256 from FIPS 180-4 in a fresh file (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/independent_audit_sha.py), importing and copying nothing from the repo or scratchpad, and DERIVING the IV and K constants from the square/cube roots of the first 64 primes rather than transcribing them. It matches hashlib on 402 messages (one- and two-block, exercising a non-IV chaining value). Under the repo's own stated convention (h = IV + compress_R(IV, W0..W15), sixteen arbitrary big-endian words, no padding), all three blocks hit their targets at R=19 exactly, and at R=18 and R=20 they miss; a sweep of R = 1..32 shows R=19 is the ONLY matching round count for each, so there is no round-count degeneracy. Without the feed-forward the raw 19-round state does not equal the target, so the match is not an artifact of a rigged output convention. The claimed context conditions are confirmed on state I recomputed myself: a4 = a5 = 0 and e8 = e9 = 0xFFFFFFFF in all three, and the collapsed residual Maj(a4,a3,a2) - a3 = 0 (i.e. a3 a submask of a2, since Maj(0,a3,a2) = a3 & a2) in all three. The bitwise probability claim is exactly right: eps == 0 under modular subtraction holds iff Maj(v,a3,a2) = a3 as words, which fails per bit only when v_i = a2_i != a3_i, giving 3/4 per bit and (3/4)^32 = 1.0045e-4 for ANY v, a 431,440x gain over 2^-32. The reported counts are internally consistent (4,270,445/16,777,216 = 0.25454 solutions per swept a0, implying a C0-survivor rate of 0.6340, matching the 0.634^2 = 0.402 figure; expected 429 preimages vs 395 observed, 1.6 sigma). Judgement: a block whose internal state has a4 = a5 = 0 is a fully legitimate preimage. The problem solved is unchanged -- given a target fixed in advance, find any W in {0,1}^512 with IV + compress_19(IV,W) = target -- and a4=a5=0 is a property of where the attacker chose to search, not a relaxation of the problem, exactly as fixing internal-state conditions is standard in every message-modification attack since Wang. I independently constructed the family from scratch (2000/2000 random a-chains, including random nonzero v): the a-chain-to-W map is a bijection, twelve of sixteen words stay free, so the family holds ~2^384 blocks against 2^256 targets, i.e. ~2^128 expected preimages per target inside it -- no coverage obstruction. The model is identical to the paper's and to Zaikin's: real IV, feed-forward kept, no padding, not free-start and not a pseudo-preimage.

(Also: discarding a genuine W = 0xFFFFFFFF as MISS is a conservative 2^-32 loss, harmless, but note that 0xFFFFFFFF is simultaneously the table sentinel and the value forced into e8/e9 -- keep those namespaces separate in any rewrite.)

summary:
Verdict: the result is real and the construction is new as a composite, but neither of its two ingredients is new, and the project itself had already written down both levers and named this exact search as its next experiment.

I independently verified the substance first. All three sample preimages pass /home/administrator/sha/publish/code/verify_r19.py at -r 19 ("result: OK"). I re-derived the residual by hand and got eps = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 exactly, for every v, confirming the "any v" form of claim (2); a 2^24-sample test gives eps==0 rates of 0.97-1.02 x (3/4)^32 at four values of v, and at v=0 I asserted eps==0 <=> a3 submask of a2. So the claim's arithmetic holds.

(1) Literature. Both absorption levers are established SHA-2 preimage technique. Ch absorption is verbatim in Aoki-Guo-Matusiewicz-Sasaki-Wang (ASIACRYPT 2009): "If x is 1 (all bits are 1), then IF(1, y, z) = y which means z does not affect the result" -- they even anticipate the partial-mask variant. Maj degeneracy is formalized in the current state of the art, Guo-Li-Liu-Wang-Zhang (EUROCRYPT 2026, eprint 2026/353), Proposition 11 / Eq. (43): a Maj output bit is deterministic when two input bits agree, and Remark 3 calls these "auxiliary conditions... to absorb propagation in the Ch and Maj functions". What I could NOT find anywhere is the use these are put to here: collapsing a 32-bit modular consistency residual into a bitwise (3/4)^32 filter. In the published corpus absorption always serves neutral-word independence across a chunk split, never the degeneration of a final matching check. That is architectural -- the residual being collapsed only exists in this project's own attack shape (backward chain + sigma0(u)-u table + provisional W9hat + fixed-point iteration), which has no counterpart in the MITM/biclique line. So: same primitives, new target; the composite is genuinely new.

(2) This project. paper_r20_barrier.tex section "A Context Family that Removes a_2 from C0" already identifies both routes, already proposes e8=0xFFFFFFFF reached by choosing a8 via a formula character-for-character identical to super_degenerate.py's make_ctx, and already ran the same isolation experiment. The diagnostics note u_reparam_and_g_count_20260726.md goes further and sets this as its literal "Next experiment": "Search context relations for one that makes a whole constraint degenerate... identify the Ch/Maj masks a constraint passes through and saturate them via context words." The new claim therefore EXTENDS rather than contradicts -- and it extends at precisely the point the project had marked as blocked. The note had dismissed the Maj lever because "a_4 = a_3... ties a context word to an absorbed unknown... recorded as a structural observation, not as an attack step." The new family escapes that by tying two free CONTEXT words (a4=a5=v) and then, instead of forcing the residual to zero, keeping it and showing it is bitwise. That inversion is the actual contribution.

Two things to fix in any writeup. First, the claim bundles three conditions but the labor divides: {a4=a5, e9=-1} give triangularity (r19_variants.log reaches 0.4013/survivor with e8 random), and e8=-1 alone buys the submask collapse -- the rates separate cleanly, 2^-22.0 without it versus 2^-15.4 with it. Second, "any v" is only exercised at v=0; super_degenerate.py hardcodes ctx={4:0,5:0} and asserts it.

Finally, the consequence the task did not ask about but that dominates: this supersedes the project's own published headline of 2^38.3 by about 2^23, so paper_r19_final.tex's abstract and comparison table are now materially understated. R=20 is not affected -- super_r20.log shows C3==0 never fires (0 of 6,789 submask hits), exactly as the barrier note predicts.

findings.claim: The measured result is real: all three sample preimages verify against the project's independent standalone verifier, and the (3/4)^32 statistic reproduces.
findings.evidence: Ran /home/administrator/sha/publish/code/verify_r19.py (stdlib-only, does not import attack code) on all three claimed W blocks at -r 19: all three print "result: OK" against their stated targets (ffff..., 0000..., bd4ed1b2...). Separately I re-derived the residual symbolically and confirmed numerically over 2^24 samples per v: eps==0 rate is 1.0228e-04 (v=0), 9.6977e-05 (v=0xffffffff), 1.0037e-04 (v=0xdeadbeef), 1.0109e-04 (v=0x5a5a5a5a) vs predicted (3/4)^32 = 1.0045e-04. For v=0 I asserted eps==0 <=> (a3 & ~a2)==0 exactly. So both the preimages and the probability claim hold.

findings.claim: PRIOR ART (literature): the Ch absorption lever (e8=e9=0xFFFFFFFF making Ch(-1,y,z)=y) is textbook SHA-2 preimage technique, published in 2009 and used for exactly the same purpose of removing a dependence.
findings.evidence: Aoki, Guo, Matusiewicz, Sasaki, Wang, "Preimages for Step-Reduced SHA-2", ASIACRYPT 2009 (eprint 2009/477). I extracted the PDF text; the paper states verbatim: "Message stealing makes use of the absorption property of the function IF(x, y, z) = xy XOR x'z. If x is 1 (all bits are 1), then IF(1, y, z) = y which means z does not affect the result of IF function in this case; similarly when x is 0 (all bits are 0), y does not affect the result." It even anticipates the partial-mask variant: "When we want to control partial output (few bits), we need to fix the corresponding bits of x instead of all bits of x." And Fig. 3 caption: "provided that the IF functions absorb the appropriate inputs". Their mechanism for reaching the all-ones state is the same class of move (fix E_{i+2} to all 1s). This lever is not new.

findings.claim: PRIOR ART (literature): the Maj degeneracy lever (two inputs equal => third input absorbed) is also established, and is formalized as an explicit absorption condition in the current state of the art.
findings.evidence: Guo, Li, Liu, Wang, Zhang, "Dual-Syncopation Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks: New Results on SHA-2", EUROCRYPT 2026 (eprint 2026/353). Extracted text, Proposition 11 / Eq. (43): the Maj output bit is deterministic "if X[i] in X^o, Y[i] in Y^o, Z[i] in Z^#, and X[i] = Y[i]" -- i.e. when two inputs agree at a bit, the third is absorbed, which is exactly Maj(x,x,y)=x at bit level. Remark 3 names it: "The condition imposed in the above is called auxiliary condition, which is used to prevent propagation in the carry vector of modular addition, or to absorb propagation in the Ch and Maj functions." So neither of the two absorption primitives used here is novel to the field.

findings.claim: PRIOR ART (this project): paper_r20_barrier.tex ALREADY publishes both levers, the identical e8=0xFFFFFFFF-via-a8 construction, and the identical isolation experiment. The new claim is not the discovery of the levers.
findings.evidence: /home/administrator/sha/publish/paper_r20_barrier.tex lines 361-381, section "A Context Family that Removes $a_2$ from C0": "The variable $a_2$ reaches the C0 target by exactly two routes: the term $\Ch(e_8,e_7,e_6)$ with $e_6 = a_2 + T_1^{(6)}$, and $\Maj(a_4,a_3,a_2)$ inside $T_1^{(5)}$. Both are maskable by context choice. Setting $e_8 = \texttt{0xFFFFFFFF}$ (reachable by choosing $a_8$, since $e_8 = a_4 + a_8 - \Sig{0}(a_7) - \Maj(a_7,a_6,a_5)$) collapses $\Ch(e_8,e_7,e_6)$ to $e_7$; setting $a_4 = a_3$ collapses $\Maj(a_4,a_3,a_2)$ to $a_3$." The e8 formula is character-for-character the one super_degenerate.py make_ctx() uses at line 93. The paper also already ran the isolation test: "with a random context, or with either condition alone, essentially every $a_2$ gives a distinct target; with both conditions the count is exactly one in each of four trials." Same structure as the new r19_variants.log isolation test.

findings.claim: PRIOR ART (this project): the diagnostics note names this exact search as its stated "Next experiment", and gives the method. Conception of the technique is fully prior; the new work is its successful execution.
findings.evidence: /home/administrator/sha/CODEXSHA/r20_oracle_free_proposed/diagnostics/u_reparam_and_g_count_20260726.md, section "## 4. Next experiment": "Search context relations for one that makes a whole constraint degenerate rather than merely a2-free. The a2-free family shows the method: identify the Ch/Maj masks a constraint passes through and saturate them via context words." The same file, section 2, gives the measurement table ("a4 = a3 AND e8 = 0xffffffff : 1, 1, 1, 1 <- a2 eliminated") and the closing line of section 3: "the a2-free family above is the first evidence that constraint structure is attacker-shapeable at all."

findings.claim: WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW, part 1: the new construction resolves the specific blocker the project had recorded as fatal, by tying two CONTEXT words together (a4=a5=v) instead of tying context to an unknown (a4=a3). This is a real conceptual step, not a restatement.
findings.evidence: paper_r20_barrier.tex line 370-373 recorded the blocker: "The second condition ties a context word to an absorbed unknown, so the context constants would have to be rebuilt for every candidate $a_3$; it is recorded as a structural observation, not as an attack step." The new family sidesteps this entirely: a4 and a5 are both free context words, so nothing is rebuilt per candidate. The price is that Maj(a4,a3,a2) no longer collapses to a3 -- and instead of treating that as failure, the new work keeps the residual and shows it is bitwise. This is the step the project had not taken.

findings.claim: WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW, part 2: collapsing a 32-bit modular consistency residual to a BITWISE condition with probability (3/4)^32 appears nowhere in the literature I could find. In the published corpus, Ch/Maj absorption serves neutral-word independence across a chunk split, never the degeneration of a final matching check.
findings.evidence: Targeted searches for a final matching/consistency check reduced from a 32-bit word match to a bitwise or submask condition, and for a (3/4)^n per-bit filter in hash preimage cryptanalysis, returned nothing relevant. In Aoki et al. absorption enables message stealing (moving W_{i+3} across steps while preserving neutrality); in eprint 2026/353 it controls syncopation propagation. Neither converts a hard 32-bit equality into a weak per-bit filter. The reason it does not appear is architectural: the underlying attack here (backward chain from target, 16 GB sigma0(u)-u inversion table, provisional W9hat, fixed-point iteration, one exact 32-bit self-consistency test) is this project's own construction and has no counterpart in the MITM/biclique line, so there is no prior setting in which this particular residual exists to be collapsed. The composite -- same primitives, new target -- is the novel object.

findings.claim: The claim statement bundles three conditions as jointly producing both effects; the actual division of labor is cleaner and should be stated precisely, because claim (1) does NOT need e8=0xFFFFFFFF.
findings.evidence: r19_variants.py builds its base context fully at random (line 163: base = {r: int(x) for r, x in zip(range(4,11), rng.integers(...))}) -- e8 is NOT forced. Its two toggles are only with_a5 (a5=a4) and with_e9 (e9=-1), and the "both" row still reaches 0.4013-0.4016 triangular solutions per survivor with e8 random (r19_variants.log lines 17, 29, 38). So triangularity/iteration-freedom comes from {a4=a5, e9=0xFFFFFFFF}, which kill a3 from the C1 target via Maj(a5,a4,a3)=v and Ch(e9,e8,e7)=e8. The third condition e8=0xFFFFFFFF is what buys claim (2) alone. The rate difference confirms it: r19_scale.log (no e8=-1) gets 33 preimages / 134,217,728 a0 = 2^-22.0, whereas super_degenerate.py (with e8=-1) gets 2^-15.4.

findings.claim: The "any v" generalization in claim (2) is algebraically sound, but was only exercised end-to-end at v=0; the script hardcodes v=0 despite the docstring stating the general family.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py make_ctx() line 89: ctx = {4: 0, 5: 0}, and run() line 111 asserts a4 == 0 and a5 == 0. Deriving eps by hand: with e8=-1, Ch(e8,e7,e6)=e7=a3+T1_7, and T1_5 = v - Sigma0(v) - Maj(v,a3,a2) while T1_5|_{a2=a3=0} = v - Sigma0(v) (since Maj(v,0,0)=0), so eps = W9conv - W9hat = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 for every v -- confirming the claim as stated. At v=0 this is (a3&a2)-a3 = -(a3&~a2), the submask form. My 2^24-sample test confirms the (3/4)^32 rate at four values of v including v=0xffffffff. Recommend running the full pipeline at one nonzero v before publishing the family as 2^32-sized.

findings.claim: CONSEQUENCE: the result supersedes the published paper's own headline number by about 2^23, so paper_r19_final.tex's abstract and comparison table are now materially understated.
findings.evidence: paper_r19_final.tex Table \label{tab:comparison} lists "\textbf{This work} & \textbf{19} & ${\approx}2^{32}$ per attempt, ${\approx}80$ attempts & random; all-ones & \textbf{seven}" -- i.e. 2^38.3 swept a0 per preimage and seven preimages total. The new family measures 2^15.4 per preimage with 395 verified across 4 targets in 6 CPU-seconds, and 99 against the all-ones digest in ~1.5 CPU-seconds. Every submask hit is a preimage at R=19 (395 submask -> 395 verified), because eps==0 is the exact and only remaining consistency condition once C0/C1/C2 are solved triangularly. The paper's central quantitative claim, its GPU-hours framing, and its Zaikin comparison all need rewriting.

findings.claim: The new family does NOT contradict the R=20 barrier note; it is consistent with it. R=20 remains unbroken.
findings.evidence: super_r20.log, target 400: the family transplants cleanly to R=20 (0.4015 triangular solutions per survivor, submask rate 9.9394e-05 matching (3/4)^32) but "C3 == 0 : 0   C3_lo==0 0" over 6,789 submask hits and 268M swept a0, and 0 verified preimages. That is exactly what paper_r20_barrier.tex predicts: the family makes each step cheap but leaves C3 as a full independent 2^-32 check, matching the note's g-count argument that "total cost 2^(32g) regardless of how the work is distributed". Note also the R20 run appears truncated (target 401 header with no results), so that lane is incomplete.

findings.claim: Terminology hazard for any writeup: this project already uses "absorb"/"absorber" in a different technical sense than the literature does, and conflating them will confuse referees.
findings.evidence: In paper_r20_barrier.tex and the project notes, "absorber" means a global table inverting a map such as Gamma(a0)=a0+g(a0) or sigma0(u)-u, letting a constraint solve for an unknown by lookup (see Corollary \label{cor:absorb}, "Every constraint has a global absorber", and the table at lines 579-592). In Aoki et al. and eprint 2026/353, "absorption" means a Boolean function losing a dependence on one of its inputs. The new construction uses BOTH senses simultaneously -- Ch/Maj absorption in the literature sense to enable table absorption in the project sense -- so the two must be named apart explicitly.

findings.claim: Context on how large the practical margin is: the prior practical state of the art for the SHA-256 compression function is very recent and very expensive, which makes the 1.5 CPU-second figure the headline rather than the 2^15.4.
findings.evidence: paper_r19_final.tex records Zaikin (Constraints 2026) at 19 rounds, all-ones digest, "18 h 33 min on 192 CPU cores" for one preimage (~3,562 CPU-hours), via parameterized Kissat in Cube-and-Conquer. Search confirms Zaikin's abstract frames the prior baseline as: "In 2012, 28-step MD5, 23-round SHA-1, and 16-round SHA-256 compression functions were reduced to SAT and inverted by Conflict-Driven Clause Learning solvers, yet no progress in this area has been made since then." Against that, 99 verified preimages on the same target in ~1.5 CPU-seconds is roughly a 10^10 improvement in cost per preimage. (One search summary also asserted practical preimages were known up to 18 steps with none at 19+; I could not verify that sentence in a primary source and would not cite it without checking.)

findings.claim: 2^38.3 swept a_0 is the right paper-side baseline: it is literally the product of the paper's own Table 1 entries, and it reconciles with the paper's micro-rate model.
findings.evidence: paper_r19_final.tex:1071 Table 1 reads "~2^32 per attempt, ~80 attempts"; 80 = 1/mu-hat with mu-hat = 3/240 = 1.25e-2 (line 775). 80 x 2^32 = 3.44e11 = 2^38.32. Cross-check from the paper's own per-stage rates (Table tab:stats, lines 688-696): 0.6337 survivors/a0 x 1.6e-5 fixed points/survivor x 1.0e-3 lo x 2.0e-4 hi = 2.0e-12 preimages/a0 = 2^38.8 -- agrees within 0.5 bits. The abstract's cost unit is the same one ("Each attempt sweeps one 32-bit variable, costs O(2^32) table lookups"), so comparing in swept a_0 is the paper's own accounting.

findings.claim: "42,474 swept a_0 per preimage" is NOT like-for-like -- it is conservative by 20.4x, because a swept a_0 in the new family costs 2.04 table lookups against 41.6 in the paper's harness.
findings.evidence: publish/code/h100_extended.py:192-215: `for sk in range(len(seeds_a2))` (K_seeds=4, default at line 345) wraps `for it in range(max_iter)` (8, line 202), and each iteration issues two full-width `tlookup` calls (lines 206, 214). No break, no compaction -- verified by grep: the only `torch.where` calls (217, 297-298) freeze lanes, they do not retire them. So per C0 survivor: 4 x 8 x 2 = 64 lookups, plus 1 per swept a_0 for C0: 1 + 0.6337*64 = 41.56. New family (super_degenerate.py:138,144,150): 1 + 0.6337 + 0.6337^2 = 2.0353. Ratio 20.42. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the 41.6 model from the paper's own two wall times: my count predicts K_seeds=4 / K_seeds=0 work ratio 41.56/11.14 = 3.73; the paper measures 89 s vs 25 s = 3.56 (line 829, which the paper itself attributes to "the 4x increase in inner-loop work"). Both configs imply the same H100 gather rate (2.005e9 and 1.914e9 lookups/s), which would be absurd (4.8e7/s) if a context were only 2^32 lookups. Consequence: the honest hardware-neutral ratio is 2^43.7 lookups/preimage vs 2^16.3 = 2^27.4 (1.8e8x), not 2^23.1 (8.7e6x).

findings.claim: The core measurement reproduces exactly, and the submask condition is not a lossy filter -- 8,128 of 8,128 candidates verified as genuine 19-round preimages across 13 contexts and 11 targets.
findings.evidence: Re-ran super_degenerate.py 19 4194304 4: 4,270,445 triangular solutions, 395 submask, 395 verified, 42,474 a0/preimage, 6.5 s -- byte-identical to the reported figures. Widened it (audit_v.py, random v, 8 targets/8 contexts): 878/878 verified, all 878 messages distinct, 38,217 a0/preimage. findings.claim: The 2^23.1 headline ratio inherits +/-1.5 bits of uncertainty from the paper-side baseline, which the paper itself does not treat as settled; the honest range is 2^21.5 to 2^25.0.

Line 778-783 warns the pooled 1.25e-2 "mixes the two arms and the screened half is enriched by construction... the control arm is the closer analogue and it produced no events" (0/120). findings.claim: The Zaikin ratio (~10^9) excludes the one-time 16 GiB table build and the warm-RAM prerequisite. For a single preimage from a cold start the honest ratio is ~6x10^4, not ~10^9.
findings.evidence: Zaikin: 18 h 33 min x 192 cores = 1.2822e7 core-seconds for one preimage. New family: 99 preimages of the all-ones digest from 2^22 a0; at my measured single-threaded 3.37e6 a0/core-s that is 1.24 core-s, i.e. 0.0125 core-s/preimage -> marginal ratio 1.02e9 = 2^29.9 (the stated ~1.5 CPU-seconds is right, slightly conservative). But table_build.log records 215 s to build the 2^32-entry 16 GiB table, which Zaikin's SAT pipeline needs no counterpart to. Cold start for ONE preimage: 215 + 0.013 = 215 core-s -> ratio 5.96e4 = 2^15.9. The billion-fold figure only materialises after amortising over >~10^4 preimages. Second unstated prerequisite: my 6.9e6 random 4-byte reads/s into the 16 GiB table requires it resident (free -g showed 21 GiB buff/cache on a 62 GiB box); cold NVMe random access would be 10-100x slower. Both belong in any published statement of the ratio. Three unfairnesses run the OTHER way and should also be stated: Zaikin's 3,560 core-hours is a single favourable draw on a problem whose solutions are 19-round preimages with probability 1/8 (paper line 1112-1114, expectation ~8x = 28,500 core-hours), his 7 days x 192 cores of failed direct attempts are excluded, and priority at 19 rounds is his (paper's own framing, abstract).

findings.claim: Restricting the context costs 2^96 of context supply and matters not at all: one context yields ~110,000 distinct preimages, and one is needed.
findings.evidence: Family free words: v = a4 = a5 (2^32), a6 (2^32), a7 (2^32), a10 (2^32); a8 and a9 are determined by e8 = e9 = 0xFFFFFFFF (super_degenerate.py:93-95). So 2^128 contexts at R=19 (2^160 at R=20, a11 free), against 2^224 for unrestricted a4..a10 -- a 2^96 reduction. Measured yield 2.550e-5 per a0 x 2^32 = 109,500 = 2^16.7 distinct preimages per context. I confirmed linearity to 2^28 (1/16 of a context): 6,855 verified from one context, of which 6,649 distinct; the 3.0% duplication is exactly the sampling-with-replacement artefact n^2/2m = 3.1% (the script draws random a0 rather than enumerating), not saturation. Family capacity 2^128 x 2^16.7 = 2^144.7 preimages available vs 1 needed. Even the R=20 requirement of 2^15.3 contexts leaves 2^144.7 of margin. Non-issue.

findings.claim: The 20-round projection of 2^47.3 swept a_0 is arithmetically correct but is a pure extrapolation: the uniform-C3 assumption it rests on is supported by ONE observed event, and zero 20-round preimages exist.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic checks: 0.6337 x 0.4015 x 1.0037e-4 x 2^-32 = 5.95e-15 -> 1.68e14 = 2^47.26; equivalently the measured R=19 figure 2^15.26 plus a full 32 bits = 2^47.26. Consistent. But c3_uniformity.log over 39 R=20 contexts and 66,774 submask candidates records exactly 1 C3-low-half hit against 1.019 expected under uniformity, and 0 full C3 hits. A Poisson 95% interval on one event is [0.025, 5.47] x uniform, which alone opens the projection to 2^44.8 - 2^52.6. Independence between the submask event and C3 is also assumed, and R=19's own history is that precisely this assumption fails: paper_r19_final.tex:656-661 measures 52-85x and 12.6-13.3x structural enhancements in the W9 halves because the iteration was seeded on partial consistency -- here the submask event forces a3's set bits to be a subset of a2's, and C3 is a function of both through W3 and W4. Total R=20 exposure so far is ~2.9e9 swept a0 = 1/58,000 of one expected preimage. Report 2^47.3 as a projection with that band, never as a cost. If it holds: 2^48.3 table lookups, ~13,900 core-hours (~3 days on Zaikin's 192 cores) or ~48 GPU-hours projecting from the paper's measured 2.0e9 lookups/s -- and it would beat paper_r20_barrier.tex's headline ("2^64 per context-equivalent", "expected total work ~2^71.4", lines 239-242) by 2^24.1 in that note's own unit.

findings.claim: "6 seconds on one CPU core" is ~1.35 cores in the headline run; the underlying rate survives a proper single-threaded measurement, so this is cosmetic but should be fixed before publication.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py 19 4194304 4 as shipped: real 6.53 s, user 8.76 s, sys 1.24 s -> ~1.53 core-seconds of CPU per wall second (numpy threading). Re-running one context at 2^28 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 / OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 / MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 gives 79.62 s elapsed at 99% CPU for 268,435,456 a0 = 3.37e6 a0 per genuine core-second, and the same 39,159 a0/preimage. So the claim holds when stated as "3.4M swept a0 per core-second, single-threaded"; it should not be stated as "6 seconds on one core" for a run that consumed 10 core-seconds.

findings.claim: The "any v" generality in the claim is real but the shipped script does not test it -- its collapsed check is hardcoded to v = 0 and asserts false for v != 0.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py:88 sets ctx = {4: 0, 5: 0} and line 156 tests sub = (A3 & ~A2) == 0, which is Maj(v,a3,a2) == a3 only at v = 0. Patching make_ctx to a random v with the same test trips the script's own cross-check at line 164 ("collapsed eps disagrees with the general formula"). Replacing the test with the general Maj(a4, A3, A2) == A3 makes it pass and reproduces the rate: 8 targets, random v per context, 878/878 verified, submask rate 1.0284e-4 vs predicted 1.0037e-4. The algebra confirms it for any v: with a4 = a5 = v, T1_5 = v - S0(v) - Maj(v,a3,a2) and W9hat uses Maj(v,0,0) = 0, so eps = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3; per bit this needs a3_i <= a2_i where v_i = 0 and a2_i <= a3_i where v_i = 1, each 3/4. The a3-independence of the C1 target also holds for any v: Maj(a5,a4,a3) = Maj(v,v,a3) = v, and Ch(e9,e8,e7) = e8 when e9 = -1. Fix the script's test rather than the claim.

findings.claim: The stronger available headline is the all-zero digest, not the all-ones one: it is Davydov et al.'s published benchmark that no SAT encoding solved at 19 rounds, and the same 2^22 sweep produced 111 verified preimages of it.
findings.evidence: super_fixed_targets.py run: all-ones 99 verified, all-zero 111 verified, both from 2^22 a0 in ~4 s total wall. paper_r19_final.tex:1091-1098 records that Davydov et al. tried four CNF encodings with Kissat at a 5000 s limit and report 19 rounds unsolved for every encoding; a 24-hour cube-and-conquer run on 16 cores solved every weakened case except the 32-bit one, i.e. at most 31 of 256 output bits, and "Their published benchmark instances fix the all-zero digest as the target." I verified one of the all-zero preimages independently with publish/code/verify_r19.py (result: OK). That is a target on which the SAT line has a published negative result, which is a cleaner claim than beating Zaikin's positive one.

summary:
The cost comparison is honest, and in the direction that matters it is conservative rather than inflated. I reproduced the measurement exactly (395 verified from 16.78M swept a_0 in 6.5 s) and extended it: 8,128 of 8,128 submask candidates verified as genuine 19-round preimages over 13 contexts and 11 targets, all messages distinct, pooled rate 39,218 swept a_0 per preimage (2^15.26). Three of the published messages check out under the repository's own standalone verifier.

On the four questions asked:

(1) 2^38.3 is the right paper-side baseline -- it is literally 2^32 x 80, the product of the paper's own Table 1 entries, and it reconciles with the paper's independent micro-rate model to within 0.5 bits. It carries +/-1.5 bits of the paper's own uncertainty (95% CI [2^36.8, 2^40.6]; control arm 0/120; dedicated runs suggest 2^36.25). So quote the ratio as ~2^23 +/- 1.5 bits, not as a point value.

(2) A swept a_0 is NOT like-for-like -- and the error favours the paper. The published harness issues 4 seed chains x 8 iterations x 2 lookups per C0 survivor with no compaction and no early exit: 41.56 table lookups per swept a_0, against 2.04 for the new family. That 20.4x is independently corroborated by the paper's own two wall times (89 s vs 25 s = 3.56x, my count predicts 3.73x, and both configs imply the same 2.0e9 gathers/s on the H100). Work-honest ratio: 2^43.7 lookups vs 2^16.3 = 2^27.4 (1.8x10^8), against the conservative 2^23.1 (8.7x10^6) in swept a_0. Publish the conservative one; state the other.

(3) Context restriction is irrelevant. The family holds 2^128 contexts (2^160 at R=20) against 2^224 unrestricted -- a 2^96 loss -- but ONE context yields ~110,000 distinct preimages and one is needed. I confirmed linearity to 2^28 a_0 with no saturation.

(4) The Zaikin ratio is the one number I would call materially misleading if published unqualified. Marginal ratio 1.0x10^9 (2^29.9) is right, but it excludes the measured 215 core-second table build and a 16 GiB warm-RAM prerequisite that his SAT pipeline has no counterpart to. For a single preimage from cold the ratio is 6.0x10^4 (2^15.9). Three other asymmetries run the other way (his figure is a 1-in-8 favourable draw, his 7 days x 192 cores of failed direct attempts are excluded, and priority at 19 rounds is his).

The 20-round projection is arithmetically correct -- 0.6337 x 0.4015 x 1.0037e-4 x 2^-32 = 5.95e-15, so 2^47.26 swept a_0, which is just the measured 2^15.26 plus a full 32 bits -- but it is not a cost, it is an extrapolation across an unobserved 2^32. The uniform-C3 assumption behind it rests on ONE observed low-half event against 1.019 expected over 39 contexts, whose Poisson interval alone opens the answer to 2^44.8-2^52.6, and R=20 exposure to date is 1/58,000 of one expected preimage. If it does hold it beats the companion note's 2^71.4 by 2^24.1 in that note's own unit, which is the reason to be strict about labelling it a projection.

Two smaller fixes: the headline run consumed ~10 core-seconds over 6.5 s wall, not 6 core-seconds (a clean single-threaded rerun gives 3.37M a_0/core-second and the same rate, so state it that way); and the shipped script's collapsed test is hardcoded to v = 0 -- the general-v form Maj(v,a3,a2) == a3 is correct and I verified it, but the script asserts false without the patch. Finally, the all-zero digest result (111 preimages of Davydov et al.'s benchmark target, which no SAT encoding solved at 19 rounds) is a stronger headline than the all-ones one.

The headline survives an adversarial audit. I reproduced the reported run bit for bit (4,270,445 triangular solutions, 395 submask, 395 verified, 16,777,216 swept a0, 42,474 a0/preimage, 6.49 s wall at 99% of one core) and every attack I made on it failed to break it.

The verification path is genuine: it rebuilds all 16 message words from the recovered state via recW and re-hashes from IV through a forward pass that never touches the solver state, with the forward model asserted against hashlib at 64 rounds. I took 263 preimages from 10 targets and pushed them through publish/code/verify_r19.py, a stdlib-only implementation that does not import the attack code: 263 OK, 0 FAIL, 263 distinct blocks. The three sample preimages in the brief also verify.

Counting is sound at the reported parameters. I instrumented an exact swept counter and got exactly 16,777,216. The 395 preimages come from 395 distinct a0 and are 395 distinct 16-word blocks; the 8,235 birthday duplicates among the random a0 draws (0.049%) produced no duplicate preimages. No filtering touches the denominator.

The eps filter is real and correctly tight in both directions: 48,000 triangular solutions with eps != 0 were rebuilt and re-hashed and none verified, while ver == sub exactly. The general eps formula re-derives correctly from scratch, and the C0/C1/C2 target algebra at lines 138/143/149 matches an independent derivation. The 16 GB table checks out (coverage 0.63337 vs 1-1/e; all 2.66M sampled hits satisfy s0(w)-w == u), and its MISS sentinel can only lose solutions, never add them. Scaling to 32 targets and 1.34e8 swept a0 gives 3,361 preimages at 2^-15.29, so the published 2^15.4 is if anything slightly conservative.

Three defects worth fixing, none of which touches the published number. The significant one is a latent inflation landmine: the batch loop sweeps a full 2^20 batch even when N < 2^20 while dividing by N, so a rerun at N=65536 reports 2,570 a0/preimage instead of 42,474 -- a 16x overstatement. The published run used N = 2^22 = 4B exactly, so it is clean, but the script should count actual sweeps. Second, idx[:50] caps verification per batch; it never binds here (uncapped rerun gives the identical 395) and is conservative. Third, the assert e[r] == eb[r] backward-chain check is a tautology that passes for any 32-byte string -- I confirmed this with all-ones, all-zeros and random bytes -- so it offers no assurance, though bc() is in fact correct.

One scope gap: the shipped script hardcodes v=0 and asserts a4==a5==0, so the "any v" half of the claim is undemonstrated. I built a generalized variant and it holds -- v=0xdeadbeef gives 410/410 and random v gives 427/427, with the internal general-eps assert still passing against the Maj(v,a3,a2)==a3 form. Finally, the comparison unit against the paper's 2^38.3 is the same "per swept a0" and understates rather than overstates the gain, since the new path costs ~2.04 table lookups per a0 against up to 16 for the iterated method.

findings.claim: Latent 2^20/N rate inflation: the batch loop `for b in range(max(N // B, 1))` sweeps a full B=2^20 batch even when N < 2^20, but every rate is divided by N. Not triggered at the reported parameters, so the headline is unaffected -- but any rerun with a smaller N silently reports an inflated number.

Demonstrated: `python3 super_degenerate.py 19 65536 2` prints `a0 65,536: survivors 663,983` (survivors exceed the claimed sweep -- the tell) and reports `2^-11.3, a0 per preimage = 2,570`, a 16x inflation of the true 2^-15.4. It never binds at the reported parameters, but it would silently under-report a more productive family -- and it makes ver==sub agreement partly an artifact of the cap not binding.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py:175. Mean submask hits per batch in the published run is 395/16 = 24.7, so the cap never engages. I reran the whole pipeline with the cap removed (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/probe2.py) and got the identical 395 verified across the same 4 targets. Direction is conservative (undercount), never inflation.

findings.claim: The backward-chain sanity check `assert e[r] == eb[r]` is a tautology and constrains nothing: bc() derives a[r-4] from exactly the relation the assert re-checks, so it passes for any 32-byte string whatsoever. It provides no assurance about bc(). (bc() is nevertheless correct -- I checked the algebra and it is confirmed end-to-end.)
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py:106 vs bc() at :68-73. bc sets a[r-4] = e[r] - (a[r] - T2(a[r-1],a[r-2],a[r-3])); run() then recomputes e[r] = a[r-4] + a[r] - T2(a[r-1],a[r-2],a[r-3]) at :105 -- algebraically the same equation. Empirically confirmed in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/probe4.py: the assert passes for h = all-ones, all-zeros, and two random 32-byte strings, each of which also yields verified preimages at the same 2.5e-5/a0 rate.

findings.claim: The 'a4 = a5 = v (any v)' generality of the claim is not tested by the shipped script, which hardcodes v=0 and asserts a4==0 and a5==0. I verified the generalization separately and it holds, but the artifact as shipped only demonstrates v=0.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py:88-92 (`ctx = {4: 0, 5: 0}`) and the guard at :111 (`assert ... a4 == 0 and a5 == 0`); the collapsed test at :156 is hardcoded to the v=0 form `(A3 & ~A2) == Z`. Claim (2)'s eps = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 is therefore correct for general v, since per bit Maj(v_i,a3_i,a2_i)=a3_i holds with probability 3/4 for either value of v_i.

findings.claim: Verification path is genuine, not short-circuited. It rebuilds all 16 message words from the recovered state and re-hashes from IV through an independent forward pass that never touches the solver state. Confirmed by a fully independent stdlib implementation.

findings.claim: No double counting. All 395 preimages come from distinct a0 and are distinct 16-word blocks; the ~0.05% birthday duplicates in the random a0 draws produced zero duplicate preimages.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/probe2.py over the same 4 targets: ver=395, n_distinct_a0_hits=395, n_distinct_W=395, dup_a0_draws=8,235 of 16,777,216 (0.049%, matching the 2^43/2^32 birthday expectation). Triangular solutions that fail it do not hash to the target, so the collapsed condition and the general eps formula cannot both be wrong in a way that inflates the count -- the end-to-end digest check is the independent arbiter and ver == sub exactly.
findings.evidence: Control in scratchpad/probe2.py: 48,000 triangular solutions with eps != 0 were fully rebuilt and re-hashed; 0 verified. Meanwhile 4,270,445 triangular solutions yield only 395 preimages (9.25e-05), so the filter is doing real work. The general formula at super_degenerate.py:159-163 is correct: W9conv = W9base - T1_5 - S1(e8) - Ch(e8,e7,e6) is the a1-independent part of W9, matching W9hat's construction at :123-125; with e8 = -1, Ch(e8,e7,e6) = e7 kills the e6 term and eps reduces to Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 as claimed. findings.claim: The 16 GB inversion table -- the only input not self-contained in the script -- is valid, and its 0xFFFFFFFF MISS sentinel loses at most one true preimage in 2^32 (conservative, never inflating).
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/probe3.py: table has exactly 2^32 entries; on 2^22 random probes coverage is 0.63337 vs 1-1/e = 0.63212; all 2,656,559 hits satisfy s0(w)-w == u exactly. The value 0xFFFFFFFF is never attained by s0(w)-w (0/2^24 random w), so the sentinel is unambiguous as a value; only the single word w = 0xFFFFFFFF (which maps to u = 0x20000000) could be masked, and the table stores one preimage per u where ~1.58 exist, so lookups systematically undercount solutions.

findings.claim: Cosmetic/hygiene issues that mask nothing but should be cleaned before publication.
findings.evidence: super_degenerate.py:149 emits 'RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar subtract/add' on every run -- I confirmed these are benign (numpy 2.4.2 uint32 scalars wrap mod 2^32 identically to Python, checked in scratchpad/probe1.py), but they would mask a genuine warning. The `eps0` counter (:130, :165) is tallied and never printed. `c7` (:112) and Wr[12], Wr[13] (:117) are computed and unused at R=19. Also structural, not a defect: all preimages within one context share W12..W15 (visible in the printed samples, e.g. `26ffc552 07bb55bc fee16d43 f4578256` on both target-400 hits) since those words are fixed by context plus target -- the 395 are distinct blocks but a highly structured family, ~1.0e5 available per context.

findings.claim: Claim (b) is EXACTLY correct: with e8 = 0xFFFFFFFF, eps = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 (mod 2^32), and this needs only a4 = v and e8 = -1 (a5 = a4 is NOT required for it).
findings.evidence: Derived from FIPS 180-4: e_r = a_{r-4} + a_r - T2_r, hence W9 = W9base - Sigma1(e8) - Ch(e8,e7,e6) - T1_5 - a1 with T1_5 = a5 - Sigma0(a4) - Maj(a4,a3,a2), e6 = a2 + T1_6, e7 = a3 + T1_7. General residual eps = Maj(a4,a3,a2) - [Ch(e8,e7,e6) - Ch(e8,T1_7,T1_6|a3=0)]. e8 = -1 forces Ch(e8,y,z) = y identically, so the bracket collapses to (a3+T1_7) - T1_7 = a3. Checked in indep_algebra.py: 2000/2000 random 19-round executions satisfy the W9 identity; 0/4000 failures of eps == Maj(a4,a3,a2) - a3 with a4=a5=v, and 0/4000 failures with a5 drawn freely (only e8 forced).
